title: Tučepi with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Hotels, Rules
metaDescription: Planning a holiday with a dog in Tučepi, Croatia: dog beaches, restaurants, ferries, pet fees, heat, vets and EU pet passport rules, with a clear verdict.
content:
## Are Dogs Allowed on Beaches in Tučepi?

Croatia has no blanket right of access for dogs on beaches. Most municipal beaches ban them in summer, and local rules and signs decide the matter. Tučepi has a long pebble beach with a promenade, and its central, serviced sections are not meant for dogs. Dogs are tolerated on quieter, less developed pebble stretches and coves at either end of the village, but conditions change by season and by municipal decision, so check the signs on arrival.

The reliable option is the dog beach at Cvitačka in Makarska, on the Tučepi side of town about 5 km from Tučepi centre. It has a pebble shore and clear water where dogs can swim. Other dog-friendly spots on the Makarska Riviera include coves around Igrane and Baška Voda, but these are further away and vary in how openly they welcome dogs.

Carry water and a bowl for the dog, because dog-friendly coves rarely have shade, taps or bins. Pebbles get hot by midday, and sea urchins are common on rocky entries. Water shoes for the dog are a sensible purchase.

## Dogs in the Old Town, Restaurants and Cafés

Tučepi has no walled old town. Its centre is a flat seafront promenade and a harbour, and leashed dogs are fine there. The nearest historic centres are Makarska (about 5 km) and Split, where Diocletian's Palace allows leashed dogs on its stone streets. The polished marble gets slippery and hot in summer, so go early or after sunset.

Restaurants and konobas generally accept dogs on outdoor terraces. Indoor dining rooms are often off-limits, as food-hygiene rules restrict animals where food is prepared. The practical approach is to ask before sitting and to choose a table in shade. Hotels with garden restaurants are usually easiest. Supermarkets and bakeries do not admit dogs, so one adult waits outside.

## National Parks and Nature Parks Near Tučepi

Biokovo Nature Park rises directly behind Tučepi. Leashed dogs are generally accepted on its trails and roads, but the Biokovo Skywalk, the high road and the summit area are exposed, and temperatures at the top drop sharply from those on the coast. Ticks, loose stone and steep drops are the real hazards. Keep the dog on a lead and carry 1.5 litres of water per dog for any walk longer than an hour.

National parks such as Krka and Plitvice impose stricter rules, and Krka restricts dogs on its main routes. Check the park's current rules before driving there from Tučepi.

## Ferries and Catamarans With a Dog

Pets travel free on Jadrolinija ferries and passenger ships. Rules for dogs are the same on every line: a leash and a muzzle are mandatory, and dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck. Small pets under 8 kg go in a carrier, which stays on the passenger's lap or under the seat.

Catamarans are different. Dogs over 8 kg need a reserved box on the open deck, with a fee set by Jadrolinija and a mandatory reservation made through a sales office. If no box is free, switch to a conventional car ferry. From Makarska, the Jadrolinija car ferry to Sumartin on Brač takes about 50–60 minutes. Fares run from €4.10 to €6.40 per adult and €18.70 to €27.00 for a standard car depending on the season, and the dog is free.

The catamaran box system is one of those things that sounds simple until you need it in August. For a large dog, take the car ferry and skip the catamaran.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Private apartments are the most flexible choice in Tučepi. Typical pet fees are €5–€15 per night or a flat €30–€60 per stay. Some hosts charge nothing, and some refuse dogs altogether. Larger hotels, including the Bluesun hotels on the beachfront, list pet-friendly rooms and set their own fee. Always confirm the size limit, the number of dogs allowed, whether the dog can be left alone, and whether sofas and beds are off-limits. Ground-floor units with a garden or terrace are the most practical. A fenced garden means a dog can be let out before breakfast without a leash.

## Summer Heat and the Best Months to Visit

July and August bring daytime highs of 30–35°C, and pavement and pebbles can burn paws. Limit walks to before 9:00 and after 19:00 and never leave a dog in a parked car. Sea temperature reaches 24–26°C in midsummer.

The best months are May, June, September and October. Air temperatures are 20–28°C, the sea is warm enough for swimming from June to October, and beaches are quieter. Restrictions on dogs on beaches are also less strictly enforced outside peak season, although this is no guarantee.

## Vet Basics in the Makarska Riviera

Makarska has several veterinary clinics, and Split, about 60 km away, has larger clinics and emergency services. Ask your accommodation for the nearest 24-hour option on arrival. Before travel, discuss tick and flea protection. Ticks are common in scrub and on Biokovo trails, and sandflies in coastal Dalmatia can carry leishmaniasis, so a repellent collar is worth considering. Pack the dog's regular medication, a copy of vaccination records, and a basic first-aid kit with tweezers for ticks.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving In

A dog travelling within the EU needs three things: a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet. In Croatia the passport costs €10.06 plus VAT. Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment for dogs entering. Treatment is only needed for Finland, Ireland, Malta, Northern Ireland and Norway, so it matters if your route home passes through them.

A new EU regulation applies from 22 April 2026, but the rules for travellers remain almost unchanged, and existing passports stay valid. Pet passports issued in Great Britain are no longer accepted for entry into the EU. Owners from the UK, USA and other non-EU countries need an animal health certificate issued no more than 10 days before entry. Up to five pets can travel on a non-commercial trip. Drivers crossing from Slovenia, Hungary or Bosnia-Herzegovina should expect spot checks, so keep the passport in the glovebox.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Tučepi?

Tučepi scores about 6 out of 10 for dog owners. Accommodation, restaurant terraces and walks on the promenade are easy. Beach access is the weak point, because there is no dedicated dog beach in the village itself, and dogs rely on quiet coves and the Cvitačka beach in Makarska. A dog that loves to swim every day will be happier in a house with a garden and a car for short trips. Visit in May, June, September or October, book a ground-floor apartment that explicitly accepts dogs, and keep a muzzle in the bag for ferries.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Tučepi?
faq.answer: There is no widely signed official dog beach inside Tučepi itself. The best-known option is Cvitačka dog beach in Makarska, about 5 km away. Some quiet coves near the village are used by dog owners, but check local signs.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Tučepi?
faq.answer: Dogs are usually welcome on outdoor terraces and in hotel garden restaurants. Indoor dining rooms are often closed to dogs, so ask before sitting down.

faq.question: Do dogs travel free on Croatian ferries?
faq.answer: Yes, on Jadrolinija ferries pets travel free, but dogs must be on a leash and wear a muzzle. Dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck. On catamarans a paid reserved box is needed.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia from another EU country?
faq.answer: A microchip, a rabies vaccination at least 21 days old and an EU pet passport. Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment. Non-EU owners need an animal health certificate instead.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Tučepi with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October are best, with temperatures of 20–28°C. July and August often reach 30–35°C, which is risky for dogs on pebbles and pavement.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments charge for a dog in Tučepi?
faq.answer: Apartments typically charge €5–€15 per night or €30–€60 per stay. Hotel fees vary, so confirm the amount and any size limits when booking.

quickAnswer: Tučepi is moderately dog-friendly. Dogs are welcome in many apartments, on restaurant terraces and on the promenade. Most main beaches are off-limits, so plan around quieter pebble coves and the dog beach in neighbouring Makarska. Visit in May, June, September or October. You need a microchip, rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport.
